Definition: i.e. G3756 and G3361; a double negative strengthening the denial; not at all:--any more, at all, by any (no) means, neither, never, no (at all), in no case (wise), nor ever, not (at all, in any wise). Compare G3378.
BiblicalUsage: This is not one word but two, the strongest way of saying no in Greek: the ordinary negative joined to the negative of a wish or a purpose. Together they deny with an oath-like force, not ever, by no means, and the New Testament uses the pair whenever the denial must be absolute.
TheologicalSignificance: What I hold is that the double negative shows how seriously God takes His promises: when He says a thing shall not be, it shall not be.
